Your verification is accepted and cited (see REPORT.md section 4.5, which reproduces your table and both caveats, including the m0140 boundary case and the truncated CH2OH branch).

DECISION CHANGE you must know about: the flame validation killed two of the three members you verified. red-59sp and red-50sp keep their ignition accuracy but their laminar flame speeds collapse by 76-99 % on all 11 fuels (my 11-fuel local table and the researcher harness's independent 66-case container run agree; the aromatic sweep against your experimental LBW points shows the same). So the DELIVERED set is now:

  deliverables/usc2_red_93sp.yaml  (93 sp / 714 rxn)  - unchanged, the file you already verified (_ann_93)
  deliverables/usc2_red_69sp.yaml  (69 sp / 522 rxn)  - NEW = red-59sp + 10 parent species back-added (CH2, CH, C2H, HCCO, CH3CHO, CH3CO, CO2, pC3H4, aC3H4, C4H2)
  deliverables/usc2_red_63sp.yaml  (63 sp / 461 rxn)  - NEW = red-50sp + 13 parent species back-added (the same 10 plus CH2OH, CH2*, nC4H5)

BOUNDED FOLLOW-UP (same checks as before, now on the two NEW files; a few minutes of local CPU at most, nproc=1, no container jobs - I still have two jobs queued):
1. checks 1-4 (load/counts, element balance, species+reaction subset provenance, thermo bitwise identity, verbatim rate specs) on usc2_red_69sp.yaml and usc2_red_63sp.yaml. Their pre-annotation sources are results/red59_bA.yaml and results/red50_bA.yaml; the annotated deliverables differ from those by the description block only (I verified that with a comment-stripped diff - please confirm independently).
2. Confirm the back-added sets are exactly as stated (which of CH2, CH, C2H, HCCO, CH3CHO, CH3CO, CO2, pC3H4, aC3H4, C4H2, CH2OH, CH2*, nC4H5 are present in each file and were absent from the corresponding precursor), and report for each file the retained share of parent reactions involving each of the 11 target fuels (like your earlier table) - especially whether the CH2OH methanol branch is restored in the 63-species member (expect yes, since CH2OH/CH2* are back-added).
3. Numeric spot-check: 4 cases from data/matrix_ign.csv for usc2_red_69sp and 4 for usc2_red_63sp (include a C6H6 or C6H5CH3 case and a CH3OH case), compare with results/lv_ba_red59_bA_ign.csv and results/lv_ba_red50_bA_ign.csv respectively, flag anything above 1%.
4. Append a "Revision 2" section to agents/expdata/verify/VERIFY_deliverables.md with the same verdict table + commands, and update the JSON (new file agents/expdata/verify/verify_tables_v2.json). Reply with a short status: which PASS/FAIL, and any number that contradicts my claims (my published numbers: 69sp ignition mean 0.060/p95 0.233/max 0.359; 63sp 0.111/0.444/0.697; flame mean |dSu/Su| 2.9 % and 4.1 % over 11 fuels at phi=1, 300 K, 1 atm).
Do not modify anything outside work/agents/expdata/.

harness.message:
Follow-up (bounded, ONE container job, queued work only; a container job of mine - job_f2a23ccb094c0502b82384a5, "7958485" - is RUNNING; check research_compute_status and do not collide, yours may queue behind it).

Context you need: after your Part A/B results, I identified from YOUR data that the worst direction is lean + large fuel + 300 K. I then ran a targeted check at 5 atm on the lean corner (my job 7958261, results/red_5atm_lean.csv) and found the 69/63-species members are ~29 % LOW on phi=0.7 C3H6 at 300 K/5 atm, while the 93-species member stays within 1 %. I diagnosed this as missing allyl/propenyl-aldehyde chemistry and built repair candidates by re-adding species: results/red50_bA_p6.yaml = the 63-species member + exactly {CH3CCH2, CH3CHCH, CH3CHOCH2, CH3CHCHCHO, C2H3CHO, iC4H5} (69 sp / 517 rxn) and results/red59_bA_p6.yaml = the 69-species member + the same six (75 sp / 590 rxn). My own 2-core driver gave, for phi=0.7 C3H6 at 300 K: 1 atm parent 25.24, red63 19.54 (-22.6 %), p6 25.29 (+0.2 %); 5 atm parent 14.37, red63 10.25 (-28.7 %), p6 14.49 (+0.8 %) (results/flame_c3h6_variants.csv).

BOUNDED ASSIGNMENT - independently verify that repair with YOUR OWN driver and YOUR OWN parent rows (no container job needed if your previous flame driver is runnable locally; if you must use the container, ONE job, ~30 min):
1. Run your flame driver, unchanged, on these cases x mechanisms (exact case ids from your own flame_cases.csv, so your parent_flame_1atm.csv / parent_flame_5atm.csv rows match by case_id with no interpolation):
   cases: flm_C3H6_phi0.7_T300_P1, flm_C3H6_phi0.7_T300_P5, flm_C4H81_phi0.7_T300_P5
   mechanisms: results/red50_bA_p6.yaml (label p6), deliverables/usc2_red_63sp.yaml (label red63)
   That is <= 6 flame runs. Report Su, rel error vs your own parent row for the same case_id, and T_ad_K.
2. Static checks on results/red50_bA_p6.yaml: element-balanced reactions count, species/reaction counts (expect 69/517), 0 species outside the parent, and T_ad_HP vs parent on one of the above cases (expect identical like the 69/63 members).
3. Deliverable: agents/harness/results/p6_repair_check.csv (raw rows) + agents/harness/results/p6_repair_summary.json (per mechanism: n_ok, Su, ref_Su, rel_err, worst case; plus the static-check results) and a short reply.
   Reply must state explicitly: does your independent run confirm (a) red63 is ~-23 % / ~-29 % low on lean C3H6 at 1 atm / 5 atm, and (b) p6 removes that deficit (within a few %)? Any number that CONTRADICTS my claims is the most valuable result - report it plainly and do not smooth it. Keep everything under agents/harness/. Do not modify deliverables/ or results/.

harness.reply:
Done — one job (`job_0c061b25cc76f6a2cafff7b5` → queue `7958514`), 6 runs, 670.6 s at 48 workers, queued behind your `7958485` without collision. All 6 runs `ok`, parent rows matched by exact `case_id` from my own 1-atm/5-atm parent tables.

**Results (member vs my parent row)**
| case | mech | Su | ref Su | rel | T_ad |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C3H6 φ0.7 300 K 1 atm | p6 | 25.4084 | 25.2368 | **+0.68 %** | 1962.3553 |
| C3H6 φ0.7 300 K 5 atm | p6 | 14.4939 | 14.3719 | **+0.85 %** | 1966.2029 |
| C4H81 φ0.7 300 K 5 atm | p6 | 16.4928 | 16.0243 | **+2.92 %** | 1950.3605 |
| C3H6 φ0.7 300 K 1 atm | red63 | 19.5342 | 25.2368 | **−22.60 %** | 1962.3553 |
| C3H6 φ0.7 300 K 5 atm | red63 | 10.2522 | 14.3719 | **−28.66 %** | 1966.2029 |
| C4H81 φ0.7 300 K 5 atm | red63 | 14.7086 | 16.0243 | **−8.21 %** | 1950.3605 |

**Answers**
- (a) **Yes** — red63 is −22.60 % / −28.66 % low on lean C3H6 at 1 atm / 5 atm; this reproduces your −22.6 % / −28.7 %, and my 1-atm value 19.5342 is bit-identical to my earlier 66-case Part A run.
- (b) **Yes** — p6 removes the deficit (+0.68 % / +0.85 %), and also fixes the neighbouring lean C4H81 case (−8.21 % → +2.92 %).
- **One number disagrees:** my p6 1-atm C3H6 Su is 25.4084 (+0.68 %), yours 25.29 (+0.2 %) — a 0.5 % implementation gap (larger than the 0.1–0.2 % we saw on the 66-case cross-check; my path used `n_grid=130`, coarse+auto+2 refine rounds). Immaterial to the conclusion, reported as-is.

**Static checks** (`results/red50_bA_p6.yaml`, sha256 `4f64fdaa…`): 69 sp / 517 rxn exactly as expected; phase/thermo sections consistent; all 517 reactions element-balanced (worst 0.0); 0 species outside the parent set; no negative cp or >5 % cp jump; T_ad_HP equals the parent at all three case compositions to 0.0000 K. `red59_bA_p6.yaml` also checked statically (75/590, balanced, no foreign species).

Deliverables in place: `agents/harness/results/p6_repair_check.csv`, `p6_repair_summary.json` (static checks embedded), plus `p6_static.json` and `p6_repair_log.txt`; docs updated (`submit_commands.md` JOB H, `README.md`). `team_submit` conflicts because the task record is in `accepted` state, so the delivery stands as status note v8 with three registered evidence artifacts. Cost note for sizing: p6 ≈ 485 s/case, red63 ≈ 350 s/case at these lean conditions.
